findings.claim: The enum formatter template reverses the target-framework guard: it emits ExcludeFromCodeCoverage only for NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK, where the attribute is unavailable, and omits it on other targets. This breaks enum formatter coverage exclusion on modern targets and can make generated enum formatters fail to compile on the older targets.

receipt_plan.detail: Run CodeCoverageExclusionTests.ExcludeAttributeIsGuardedForTargetsWhereItIsUnavailable; the generated enum formatter contains the attribute behind '#if NETSTANDARD2_0 || NETFRAMEWORK', so its guardedCount is zero and the assertion fails. Also inspect that generated enum source: the preprocessor symbol must be negated to match the other templates.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Decorate every generated formatter, resolver, and formatter helper unconditionally where ExcludeFromCodeCoverage exists, with no setting; omit the attribute only on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Keep the same default-on decoration for all generated types, but also add an opt-out generator/MSBuild option that suppresses emission of the attribute when a consumer disables it.
